'''''Silene noctiflora''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]] known by the common names '''night-flowering catchfly''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''nightflowering silene'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SINO|taxon=Silene noectiflora|accessdate=15 November 2015}}</ref> and '''clammy cockle'''. It is native to Eurasia, but it is known on other continents as an [[introduced species]] and sometimes a [[weed]]. In North America, it is a common weed of [[Cereal|grain crops]] in the Canadian prairie provinces and in much of the United States.<ref name=nappo>[http://www.nappo.org/PRA-sheets/Silenenoctiflora.pdf North American Plant Protection Organization] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106114402/http://www.nappo.org/PRA-sheets/Silenenoctiflora.pdf |date=2009-01-06 }}</ref> It grows in fields and in other disturbed habitat.

==Description==
[[File:Wild Night-Flowering Catchfly in Behbahan.jpg|alt=Wild Night-Flowering Catchfly in Behbahan|thumb|Wild Night-Flowering Catchfly in [[Behbahan]]]]
The night-flowering catchfly is an annual herb producing a hairy, glandular stem up to about 75 or 80 centimeters in maximum height. It is sticky in texture. The hairy, widely lance-shaped leaves grow in opposite pairs and are up to 14 centimeters long and 5 wide, the largest ones located low on the stem. The flowers are nocturnal,<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242000798 Flora of North America]</ref> and occur in an open cyme of up to fifteen blooms, each borne on an erect [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]. The flower is encapsulated in a hairy calyx of fused [[sepal]]s lined with a netlike pattern of veining. The five petals are white to pink and each has two lobes at the tip. They measure up to 2.5 centimeters wide when fully open. The fruit is a yellowish-brown capsule with six chambers which splits open to release the seeds.<ref name=NatureGate>{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/night-flowering-catchfly |title=Night-flowering Catchfly: ''Silene noctiflora'' |publisher=NatureGate |accessdate=2013-12-30}}</ref>

==Ecology==
As night falls the flowers of the night-flowering catchfly open and release a strong fragrance which attracts night-flying moths which feed on the copious nectar and pollinate the plant.<ref name=NatureGate/>

==Research==
Besides being a competitive weed, the night-flowering catchfly is host to some [[Plant pathology|plant pathogens]] that can spread to crop plants, including [[tobacco streak virus]] and [[Lychnis ringspot virus]].<ref name=nappo/>

The [[mitochondrial genome]] of this species has been sequenced. It is 6.7 megabases long, which is very large compared to some other ''Silene'' species such as [[Silene vulgaris]] (0.43 megabases), is one of the largest sequenced plant mitochondrial genomes (the largest is [[Silene conica]] at 11.3 megabases), and consists of 59 small [[chromosomes]].<ref name=genome>[http://www.plosbiology.org/article/info%3Adoi%2F10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.1001241 Mitochondrial genome study]</ref><ref name=ncbi>[https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/labs/virus/vssi/#/virus?SeqType_s=Nucleotide&VirusLineage_ss=Viruses,taxid:33090 NCBI sequenced plant mitochondrial genomes]</ref>
